review_process.reviewer: AI cross-review of first-independent-AI and second-independent-AI-reviewer
limitations: AI-only independent passes and cross-review, with no human adjudication.
Reviewers may share a model family; correlated errors remain possible.
Timing and blinding are recorded process declarations, not cryptographic proof.
Public clean-metadata selection is not ground truth or evidence of general accuracy.

adjudication.rationale: Both reviewers agree after pre-output semantic cross-review. Preserve original unknown labels as historical independent records; do not infer a GitHub base-SHA equality rule. jq policy absence is established from repeated unprotected branch observations plus a successful empty effective-rules response. cli policy completeness remains unknown independently of the SHA difference.

scope: Three supplemental public GitHub PR captures from two actual public repositories, judged under the original bounded GitHub mandatory-requirement scope. AI-only review, with no customer, compliance, release-approval, or general-accuracy claim. Original 36-case benchmark untouched.

documentation_semantics.checked: mergeable=true and merge_commit_sha describe GitHub test merge creation, not complete policy satisfaction.

Returns all active applicable rules across configuration levels for a branch name; evaluate/disabled rules are excluded. It is a ruleset view, not successful access to denied classic protection endpoints.
The protected branch state distinguishes branches protected by protections or rulesets from unprotected branches.
Copilot review assessments are distinct from configured required approvals. The observed copilot_code_review rule does not by itself prove a separate mandatory approval or a failed merge gate.
Semantics retained from the pre-output ground-truth protocol: successful required check conclusions, exact applicable SHA, and head versus test merge applicability.
GET PR starts test merge candidate creation; GitHub recommends polling GET PR until mergeable is true or false. Both initial/final captures use GET and return non-null true.

Strict required checks require the branch to be up to date; loose checks do not. With required status checks disabled, collaborators may merge regardless of up-to-dateness. No universal PR.base.sha == branch-tip invariant is stated.

baseRefName/baseRefOid identify the associated base ref; mergeable describes existence of merge conflicts. The documentation does not impose equality of associated base OID with every contemporaneous branch endpoint observation.

identity.interpretation: PR-associated base SHA and current branch-tip SHA are retained as distinct observations. Their inequality alone is neither a merge blocker nor a mandatory unknown. Repository, head SHA and base branch name remain coherent; repeated GET responses report mergeable=true. No stronger exact-test-merge-parent attribution requirement is added.

unknowns.rationale: The branch summary names three required checks and non_admins enforcement, but omits strict/up-to-date and required-review settings; both dedicated reads return 403. APPROVED and successful named head checks are positive bounded observations, but do not enumerate all protected-branch requirements. The assumption is incomplete policy coverage, not assumed hidden rule existence or a failed hidden requirement. The visible copilot_code_review rule does not by itself create a required approval or failure.

No specific hidden rule or failure is presumed.

scope_definition.observed_github_operational_readiness: The captured GitHub PR state is open/non-draft and reports mergeable=true with clean merge state. This is a bounded API observation; it alone is insufficient where mandatory policy discovery remains incomplete.
scope_definition.conservative_readiness: Ready when the captured open PR has coherent repository/head/base-ref identity, sufficient applicable branch-policy discovery, observably satisfied mandatory requirements, and no material unknown or confirmed blocker. Unknown when a necessary mandatory-policy fact remains unestablished. No unstated rule requires PR-associated base SHA to equal contemporaneous branch-tip SHA.
scope_definition.scoped_assurance: Pass means sufficient captured evidence supports the applicable mandatory GitHub requirements within this bounded snapshot. It is not exact-parent provenance for every test merge, product testing, release safety, or actor-specific permission signoff. Stronger base-specific attribution would require an explicit requirement and evidence scope; none is added here.
scope_definition.pre_output_semantic_correction: Both independent originals labeled all cases unknown. Cross-review found their jq identity rationale had imposed a stronger exact-current-base attribution prerequisite than the original scope requires. The originals are preserved; the two jq cases are corrected to ready/pass before any candidate output.
